name: Mystery Flesh Pit National Park
note: Fan work, rendered by the same engine as chicago.html and nyc.html. Mystery Flesh Pit National Park is Trevor Roberts's project (mysteryfleshpitnationalpark.com); nothing of his is used, copied or redistributed - tools/make-fleshpit.py generates fleshpit-osm.json (the West Texas surface, the orifice, the park's facilities and the Anodyne works) from a seed, and this file holds the districts, the landmarks, the viewpoints and the pit itself. Everything below the rim is built by src/fleshpit/organism.js from the "pit" block at the end of this file; the page steers its own camera down the shaft (src/fleshpit/camera.js), which no other city does. Positions are [lat, lon].

landmarks.name: The Orifice
landmarks.info: The way in. A vent forty metres across when a Jackson Surveying crew drilling for oil broke into it in 1973; the Anodyne Corporation widened it to 520 m, poured the collar round the lip and opened it to the public in 1976. The pink at the bottom of the funnel is not stained rock. Everything the park ever sold - the tours, the ballast, the resort - came out of this hole.

landmarks.name: Upper Visitor Center
landmarks.info: Opened 1976 and rebuilt in 1989 after the first expansion. Orientation film every twenty minutes, the rim exhibit, and the desk where you were weighed and told the rules before you went down.

landmarks.name: Shaft 1 Headframe
landmarks.info: One of four. The cages ran 520 m to the Throat in four and a half minutes, sixty visitors at a time, and the counterweight ran in the same shaft.

landmarks.name: Monorail Terminal
landmarks.info: The Pit Rim Monorail opened in autumn 2006, nine months before the incident, and ran the rim from the visitor center to the works platform. It carried 1.2 million people in its only full season.

landmarks.name: Anodyne Extraction Works
landmarks.info: Amniotic ballast came up here: pumped from the pods 1,200 m down, settled, refined on site, and trucked to Odessa. The park was the tenant, not the landlord - Anodyne held the extraction lease until 2007.

landmarks.name: Flare Stack
landmarks.info: What the works could not sell, it burned. The flare was visible from Gumption on a clear night, which is how most of the county knew the pit was still working.

landmarks.name: Entrance Station
landmarks.info: Twelve miles of park road from Gumption, TX. Admission in 2006 was $12 a vehicle, or $30 with a Throat tour.

landmarks.name: Gumption Flat Campground
landmarks.info: Forty-two sites on the flat, far enough west that the ground noise is only audible at night. The Park Service advised against tents in the first week of July, when the pit draws hardest.

landmarks.name: The Amphitheatre
landmarks.info: Ranger talks at dusk, with the orifice behind the stage. 'Everything you can see from this seat is alive' was the opening line of the standard programme.

landmarks.name: Permian Basin pumpjacks
landmarks.info: The oil field the pit was found in. Most of these wells were drilled before 1973 and most were still nodding in 2007; the leases round the park paid better than the park did. The ones nearest the rim were capped in 1981 when the crews noticed they were pumping something warm.

landmarks.name: Anodyne billboards
boards: NOW DAILY  ·  ASK AT THE DESK
landmarks.info: Anodyne's billboards on the park road. The company sold the pit the way the county sold everything else: loud, early and in capital letters. The Park Service took over the signs in 1981 and kept the billboards, because the billboards worked.

landmarks.name: Caver Coop
landmarks.info: The mascot, drawn in 1976 to sell a hole in the ground to families with small children. He wears a hard hat, holds the rail and smiles about it. The Park Service retired him in 1983 and put him back in 1991 because attendance had fallen.

landmarks.name: Park entrance sign
landmarks.info: The sign every family photograph starts with. Poured stone and routed cedar, to the Park Service's standard drawings, 1981.

landmarks.name: Visitor Center Parking
landmarks.title: VISITOR PARKING
landmarks.info: Four hundred and twelve stalls, full by ten on any summer Saturday. The rangers' rule of thumb was that a car still here after closing was a search, not a ticket.

landmarks.name: Overflow Parking
landmarks.info: The overflow, and the only place the RVs fit. On 4 July 2007 it was full for the first time since 1994.

landmarks.name: Works Lot
landmarks.title: ANODYNE PERSONNEL
landmarks.info: Anodyne's shift lot: pickups, mostly, and the crew bus. Shift change at six, two and ten, when the lot empties and fills again in a quarter of an hour.

landmarks.name: Upper Visitor Center plaza
landmarks.info: The plaza between the wings: the flags, the planters, the map board, the gift shop on one side and the ticket windows on the other, and the doors in under the canopy. Everybody who went down went through here first.

pit._: the superorganism below the rim, built by src/fleshpit/organism.js. Depths are metres below the plain; the park's own surveys are quoted in the cards.

layers.name: The Collar
layers.info: Poured concrete for the first 160 m, ring-bolted into the orifice wall, with the switchback ramp and the four elevator shafts inside it. This much of the park is engineering; below it, nothing is.
signs: Report any contact to a ranger

layers.name: The Throat
layers.info: The entry tube: 360 m of muscle held open by steel stent hoops cleated into the wall, with tension cables run between them. Below the last hoop it opens into the Nexial Cavity, and the Lower Visitor Center hangs in the middle of that on a gantry and eight hydraulic rams that move all day to keep the deck level while the wall breathes round it. Shops, a cafeteria, a first-aid post and 1,100 people on a July afternoon. It is what the pit swallowed first on 4 July 2007.
signs: Trailheads by the ramps · Lifts to −1,100 m

layers.name: The Bronchial Forests
layers.info: The lungs. Two chambers off the shaft, north and south, filled floor to ceiling with bronchial growth that the surveys insisted on calling trees. Boardwalk trails, primitive and unlit past the first loop, and Septum Falls dropping 90 m through the north chamber. The air moves through here on a twenty-two minute cycle: you can hear it coming.
signs: The floor is not a floor
Spray is irritant: do not look up

layers.name: Amniotic Thermal Springs
layers.info: The springs are a cluster of ballast bulbs off the south-west of the shaft, fitted out as baths: eight of them open, graded by potency from the Main Bath, where children are welcome, down to the Libido Bath at the bottom, where they are not. Lockers at the Bath House, towels when there are towels, and the enclosed trail down from the lifts. The Commercial Extraction Lease Area on the far side is Anodyne's, and off-limits. The Gift Gardens on the east wall are Anodyne's too.
signs: NO GLASS IN THE POOL AREA

mainBath.info: The big one, and the only bath open to children: a chamber tented up into six points round a ring of fresh-air ducts, the water the palest in the springs, two red walkways looping across it and loungers round the edge. The Bath House stands on the near side. The leaflet asks bathers not to reserve the loungers, and to keep displays of affection within reason.

baths.name: Regia Bath
baths.info: The highest of the baths and the mildest after the Main Bath: blue water, a view back down over the cluster, and the queue for it.

baths.name: Gratia Bath
baths.info: A small bath close in to the long passage, and the one below which the leaflet advises consulting a physician first.

baths.name: Placito Bath
baths.info: Out on the far edge past Regia. Take care diving: the ballast crops round it are not all mapped.

baths.name: Laetis Bath
baths.info: Blue, warm and quiet, halfway down the long passage.

baths.name: Viribus Bath
baths.info: The first of the red baths. The leaflet suggests a religious, mystic or sexual wellness counsellor before going in past the yellow line.

baths.name: Cupido Bath
baths.info: The smallest of the open baths, and the one people went to in twos.

baths.name: Salus Bath
baths.info: Next to the Main Bath and down a step in potency from Placito. The Lovers Squeeze leaves from its far side.

baths.name: Libido Bath
baths.sign: Adults only · See the Conduct & Consent leaflet
baths.info: The lowest bath in the springs and the strongest water in the park, reached through the Lovers Squeeze. The Conduct & Consent leaflet at the Bath House applies.

baths.name: Undeveloped Ballast Bulb
baths.info: A bulb the park never fitted out. The leaflet encourages visitors to try the traditional bathing process by crawling into the orifice. The rangers did not.

layers.name: The Lesser Gastric Sea
layers.info: The first of the two digestive lakes, 1,600 m down and 900 m across. The gastric ferry ran from the terminal on the north shore; the Fredrick J. Agnich Memorial Dam holds the level where the sea would otherwise drain into the lower chamber. The water is not water and touching it is fatal.

layers.name: The Greater Gastric Sea
layers.info: Four times the size of the Lesser, and warmer. The Intrapark Thermal Wellness Resort stood on the shelf above the south shore: 180 rooms, none with a window, all of them booked through 2008. The Prime Labiod Junction, where the two seas meet, is the fold that opened on the night.

layers.name: The Grand Drainage Pit
layers.info: Where both seas drain. Anodyne's lower works - Little Detroit to the crews who worked it - hangs off the wall above the drain: pumps, a pipe stack running the full height of the shaft, and the last lit thing in the park. Below this the shaft goes on. The deepest anyone has been is 19,102 m, on the 1979 expedition, and that is not the bottom.

features._: the named places below the rim, each a card: src/fleshpit/organism.js places them

gullet.name: The Sand Gullet
gullet.info: The drain at the bottom of the entry tube, where the grit and the rain that came down the orifice collected. Three Anodyne pumps kept it dry. On 4 July 2007 the first two lost power in a relay fault and the backup had seized with corrosion; the gullet filled, and the water ran on into the lungs.

bulbules.name: Bronchial bulbules
bulbules.info: The glossy clusters on the bronchial trunks. The surveys never settled what they do; they swell on the in-breath, and the boardwalk rail was set back from them in 1986 after a visitor put her hand on one.

labiod.name: The Prime Labiod Junction
labiod.info: The lipped fold where the Lesser Gastric Sea gives on to the Greater. It is normally shut. On the night it flexed open and let the lower sea up the shaft.

oyster.name: Oyster's Shame
oyster.info: A fold in the chamber wall above the Lesser Sea, named by the survey crews and never renamed. A ranger's truck went into it in 2007 and is still there; the fold closed on it and did not open again.

gardens.name: The Gift Gardens
gardens.info: Retrocognitive material gestation organs, in the company's paperwork. They grow things - bone, mostly, and sometimes objects - and Anodyne harvested them on a rota from the rigs on the east wall. The harvest crews set an extraction record on the evening of 4 July 2007.

falls.name: Septum Falls
falls.info: Ninety metres of what the north bronchial chamber drains, into a plunge pool the Park Service fenced and lit. The spray is irritant; the viewing platform is upwind of it most of the cycle.

incident._: src/fleshpit/incident.js: #2007 opens the page on the night
incident.title: 4 July 2007
incident.info: Fireworks rained off, and the park kept open to midnight. At 21:16 the harvest crews' load tripped a relay; the gullet pumps stopped and the backup had seized. Water ran into the lungs and the organism began to choke. The failsafe - twenty thousand litres of aconitine - made it worse. The rams could not hold the Lower Visitor Center; at 22:12 it tore loose and fell into the Nexial Cavity, the labiod junction opened, and gastric fluid came up the orifice in columns several hundred metres high. By 23:13 it was quiet. More than 750 people died. The park did not reopen.

tunnels.name: Passage U-1
tunnels.info: Found in 1978 by the crew fitting the stents. Surveyed to 140 m; the survey line is still pinned to the floor. Past the end of the line it forks, and the survey stops.

tunnels.name: Passage U-2
tunnels.info: A low passage off the entry tube that fills with condensation on the out-breath. The grille was put in after a tour group's child went through the gap in the first one.

tunnels.name: Passage U-3
tunnels.info: Opens off the floor of the Nexial Cavity below the deck. Air moves through it on the breath, in and out; the rangers used it to tell the time of the cycle.

tunnels.name: Passage U-4
tunnels.info: Between the lungs. Sealed with a bolted bulkhead in 1986 after two surveys a year apart found it had got longer.

tunnels.name: Kellogg's Drift (W-2)
tunnels.info: Anodyne's exploratory drift towards the heart, driven with a rail and a winch through 1983 and 1984. It was abandoned when the walls began to close on the rail at night; the cart is still where the last shift left it.

tunnels.name: Passage U-7
tunnels.info: Entered twice. The second crew came back after nine hours and would not say how far they had got. It has not been entered since 1994.

tunnels.name: Passage U-8
tunnels.info: Climbs away from the Lesser Gastric Sea towards the springs. The survey line runs 50 m and ends at a bootprint.

tunnels.name: Passage U-9
tunnels.info: The widest of them. Warm air comes out of it with a smell the crews compared to a hospital laundry.

tunnels.name: Little Detroit adit (W-5)
tunnels.info: Driven from the lower works in 1991 to find somewhere else for the drain to go. It did not find anywhere. The crews at Little Detroit hang their washing in front of the grille, where it dries in an hour.

tunnels.name: Passage U-11
tunnels.info: The deepest passage the park recorded, and the only one that was sealed from the inside. The bulkhead was fitted by a crew who went in through the drain to do it.

areaColours._: the land cover here is caliche, not lawn: the engine's defaults are a city's greens

_treeSpecies: the Permian Basin's own: honey mesquite, creosote bush, soaptree yucca
